update description: The revised 'Identify needs' phase becomes a strategic enterprise-wide gatekeeper requiring proactive scanning of all data assets for reusability, assessment of operational feasibility of new collections, dynamic cost/timeliness/risk trade-offs, standardized and auditable needs-identification procedures, digital-first cross-program data asset utilization, and early digitally-enabled stakeholder engagement.
impact reasoning: This update materially expands the role from managing divisional production and dissemination strategies within a program area to acting as an enterprise-facing decision authority at the front end of statistical work. The current work-description already includes proposal development, conceptual review, source assessment, and client needs analysis, but the revised expectation requires these activities to be performed through standardized, digital, auditable, and cross-program mechanisms. The position will need to systematically examine reusable internal and external data assets before approving or recommending new collection activity; explicitly assess feasibility, automation-readiness, and operational sustainability; and apply more formal cost, timeliness, and risk trade-off frameworks in decision making. The role also shifts toward culture change leadership by enforcing digital-first practices, supporting enterprise resource optimization, and ensuring that stakeholder engagement occurs earlier and through digital channels. This increases both operational accountability and strategic influence, while requiring stronger data asset governance, digital platform literacy, and change leadership capabilities.

Strategy work will increasingly include prioritizing reuse over new collection, embedding auditable needs-assessment processes, and aligning program planning with organization-wide efficiency and automation objectives.

update description: Program launch and needs confirmation become highly evidence-driven, reuse-first, automated where possible, and explicitly tied to resource alignment, cost efficiency, transparent prioritization, decision-logging, and metadata-driven consultation processes supported by shared digital platforms.
impact reasoning: This update materially changes the EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination role from primarily leading consultative program development and responding to evolving client demand toward governing a structured consultation and prioritization regime. The role will no longer rely mainly on iterative expert judgement and bespoke accommodation of user needs; instead, it must ensure that requests are assessed through standardized digital workflows, documented decision trails, reuse-first criteria, and explicit feasibility and resource tests before new collections or modifications proceed. The Head will be expected to oversee consultation infrastructure, monitor cycle times and outcomes, enforce transparency in trade-off decisions, and set boundary conditions for when new data collection is justified. This creates both operational changes in how consultations are run and strategic changes in how program proposals, priorities, and service decisions are defended and documented.

update description: Output objective establishment is redefined to require that proposed outputs and program objectives prioritize asset reuse, automation-readiness, digital and resource efficiency, and interoperability by default. Any custom, manual, or survey-first approach must be explicitly justified. Approval shifts to an investment-style gate tied to enterprise architecture, automation pipelines, and digital resource constraints.
interdependencies: 2.1 dependent on downstream design, build, and production processes because early objective-setting now constrains acceptable methods, architectures, and resource models for development and operation.
Impacts future system development, production design, dissemination planning, and governance approval processes by requiring automation-first and interoperability-aligned choices at inception.
impact reasoning: This update changes the role from primarily preparing and recommending statistical program frameworks and resource implications to formally governing whether proposed outputs are admissible under enterprise-wide reuse, automation, and interoperability expectations. The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination will no longer only assess whether a program is statistically sound and operationally feasible, but must also determine whether it aligns with enterprise architecture, uses existing assets where possible, is automation-ready, and represents an efficient use of scarce digital resources. This introduces a more formal gatekeeping and business-case function at the front end of program planning. The role must integrate IT architecture, automation pipeline feasibility, and data governance considerations into objective-setting before projects proceed. It also increases accountability for defining acceptance criteria, documenting exceptions, and coordinating cross-functional review with subject-matter, IT, and governance leads. As a result, operational adjustments include more structured proposal review processes, stronger architectural and digital feasibility analysis, and tighter challenge of bespoke or manual approaches. The role evolves toward strategic stewardship of statistical outputs as digital products operating within enterprise constraints.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Long-term strategies will need to be reframed to embed enterprise reuse, automation readiness, interoperability, and digital efficiency as default planning criteria rather than secondary implementation considerations. Strategic planning will include early-stage screening of whether desired outputs can be supported through existing assets, shared platforms, or automated pipelines, and whether exceptions can be justified.

gaps.justification: The current wording emphasizes long-term strategic planning for statistical programs, but does not explicitly require strategic stewardship of reusable data assets, automation-first planning, or interoperability-by-design. The future role requires these criteria to shape strategy formation itself.
gaps.name: Enterprise architecture and interoperability principles
gaps.description: Knowledge of enterprise architecture standards, shared platforms, interoperability requirements, and how these constrain or enable program strategy and output design.

gaps.justification: The role must now assess strategic options against digital resource constraints and enterprise automation priorities, which goes beyond traditional program planning.
